tests.title: Pseudonymization procedure implemented
tests.description: Pseudonymization procedure implemented
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of your pseudonymization procedure. Guidance: The GDPR defines pseudonymization as a process to render data unattributable to a specific data subject unless additional information (that is kept separately) is used to reidentify the subject(s). Pseudonymization makes data identifiable if necessary, yet inaccessible to unauthorized users and allows entities to lower the risk of a potential data breach and safeguard personal data at-rest and in-transit. A pseudonym is still considered to be personal data according to the GDPR since the process should theoretically be reversible. The applicability of pseudonymization depends on a number of factors, including risk of the processed data, method of processing, and security controls in place for the data. Vanta recommends reaching out to Privacy counsel for more clarity on this topic.

controls.title: Annual Verification of DPF Compliance
controls.description: Organizations must provide follow-up procedures for verifying that the attestations and assertions they make about their EU-U.S. DPF privacy practices are true and those privacy practices have been implemented as represented and in accordance with the Principles. Where the organization has chosen self-assessment, such verification must verify that: i. its privacy policy regarding personal information received from the EU is accurate, comprehensive, readily available, conforms to the Principles, and is completely implemented (i.e., is being complied with). ii. individuals are informed of any in-house arrangements for handling complaints and of the independent recourse mechanism(s) through which they may pursue complaints; iii. that it has in place procedures for training employees in its implementation, and disciplining them for failure to follow it; iv. that it has in place internal procedures for periodically conducting objective reviews of compliance with the above. An organization must verify such attestations and assertions either through self-assessment or outside compliance reviews as follows: i. A statement verifying that the self-assessment has been completed must be signed by a corporate officer or other authorized representative of the organization at least once a year and made available upon request by individuals or in the context of an investigation or a complaint about non-compliance. OR ii. A statement verifying that an outside compliance review has been successfully completed must be signed either by the reviewer or by the corporate officer or other authorized representative of the organization at least once a year and made available upon request by individuals or in the context of an investigation or a complaint about compliance.

tests.title: Proof of media/device disposal
tests.description: Proof of media/device disposal
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that physical media is disposed of properly through certificates of sanitization or destruction. Guidance: NIST 800-88 provides guidelines for media sanitization, including methods and techniques for differing types of media. As an example, PCI DSS Requirement 9 requires cardholder data on electronic media be rendered unrecoverable when deleted such as through a secure wipe program or be physically destroyed. There are many reputable companies which provide physical media destruction services and will issue certificates of destruction upon completion, such as Data Destruction Corporation. In lieu of a third-party performing data destruction, you can perform it internally and leverage the following sample certificate: Sample Certificate of Destruction: Google docs template / Docx template. Note: Test may be marked as not relevant if no media disposal is required and has not occurred. Implementation guidance Identify any physical media (e.g., hard drives, USBs, backup tapes) that must be sanitized or destroyed due to data lifecycle policies, PCI DSS requirements, or regulatory mandates. If destruction is handled internally, use the Google Docs Template or Word Template to document the destruction. If handled externally, request a formal certificate of destruction from the service provider. File all completed certificates in a centralized compliance repository and reference relevant standards (e.g., NIST 800-88) on each form to demonstrate audit alignment. Evidence collection To collect this evidence, gather documentation that verifies proper sanitization or destruction of physical media according to recognized security standards. Obtain certificates from external destruction vendors that include media type, disposal method, date of destruction, and authorized personnel or witnesses If performed internally, complete and sign destruction certificates using approved internal templates. Ensure the evidence references compliance with NIST 800-88 and, where applicable, PCI DSS Requirement 9. Retain supporting logs, chain-of-custody documentation, or internal policy references to validate the integrity of the process.

controls.description: The company has a privacy policy available to customers, employees, and/or relevant third parties who need them before and/or at the time information is collected from the individual.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Notice and Communication of Objectives Related to Privacy

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Notice and Communication of Objectives Related to Privacy
controls.title: Privacy policy reviewed
controls.description: The company reviews the privacy policy as needed or when changes occur and updates it accordingly to ensure it is consistent with the applicable laws, regulations, and appropriate standards.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Notice and Communication of Objectives Related to Privacy

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Notice and Communication of Objectives Related to Privacy
controls.title: Privacy policy established
controls.description: The company has a privacy policy is in place that documents and clearly communicates to individuals the extent of personal information collected, the company's obligations, the individual's rights to access, update, or erase their personal information, and an up-to-date point of contact where individuals can direct their questions, requests or concerns.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Notice and Communication of Objectives Related to Privacy

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

requirements.title: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.title: Explicit consent obtained
controls.description: The company obtains, documents, and retains the explicit consent, in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, directly from an individual prior to the collection, use, or disclosure of sensitive information. Consent may be obtained through the use of either a check box, signed form.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

tests.title: Maintain data inventory map
tests.description: Maintain data inventory map
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a link or upload your most recent Data Inventory Map. Guidance: Here's a sample Data Inventory Map template. Google docs template / Excel template Note: Documenting your Records of Processing Activities (ROPA) can adequately fulfill the requirements of a Data Inventory but it is highly recommended to have a holistic approach to Data Inventory Mapping through the implementation of a Data Governance Program. This can include maintaining a structured metadata repository for databases and cloud resources, and using a discovery engine to scan for unstructured data across all environments (e.g., endpoints, cloud stores, documentation repositories, SaaS apps, etc.)

tests.title: Cookie consent manager
tests.description: Cookie consent manager
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that a cookie consent manager is implemented on your company's website. Guidance: Often, companies will surface a banner as soon as a user enters the main website with an option to modify cookie consent settings directly within the banner. Alternatively, companies can also maintain a cookie settings page on their site. You should not hide any cookie or privacy consent options, its always best to make it available, easy to find, and simple to navigate cookie consent options.

tests.title: Cookie Policy
tests.description: Cookie Policy
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a link or upload of evidence that your company has a cookie policy. It can be separate or part of your Privacy Policy. Guidance: Here's a sample template (Google docs template / Docx template).

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

requirements.title: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.title: User data collection consent obtained
controls.description: The company obtains an individual’s consent and preferences at or before the time of collection, maintains documentation in electronic and/or written format, and implements the individuals selected preferences, for information collection, use, and disclosure, in a timely fashion.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

requirements.title: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.title: User data collection consent obtained
controls.description: The company obtains an individual’s consent and preferences at or before the time of collection, maintains documentation in electronic and/or written format, and implements the individuals selected preferences, for information collection, use, and disclosure, in a timely fashion.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

requirements.title: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.title: Non-essential privacy information opt-out available
controls.description: Individuals are able to opt-in and/or out of the use of non-essential cookies, and the company does not store, alter, or copy any personal or other information for which consent has not been obtained.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Choice and Consent

controls.title: Personal information collection changes communicated
controls.description: The company provides notice when or before personal information is directly collected from the individual and/or used for a new purpose not previously identified in the privacy policies, and within a reasonable time after new information is acquired or any changes to their privacy policies or practices have been approved.

controls.title: Personal information collection reviewed
controls.description: The company's management and/or legal counsel reviews and approves the methods for the collection of personal information prior to implementation to ensure that information is obtained in a fair and lawful manner.

controls.title: Personal information reliability verified
controls.description: The company's management reviews and approves the sources of personal information, other than the individual data subject (third-parties), to ensure that sources are reliable and that the information obtained by the third-parties has been collected in a fair and lawful manner.

controls.title: Personal information policies and procedures established
controls.description: The company reviews policies and procedures as needed or when changes occur and updates them accordingly to ensure that personal information collected is: identified as either essential or optional; performed with consent (implicit or explicit) in accordance with legal and regulatory requirements; and used in alignment with and limited to the purposes identified in the privacy notice.

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: Privacy data retained
controls.description: The company's retention requirements are documented, and personal information is retained, as required, for business purposes, including to fulfill the purposes related to its collection, and/or by applicable laws or regulations.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: Data deletion requests handled
controls.description: The company validates deletion requests and once confirmed are flagged and the requested information is deleted, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: Privacy inquiries handled
controls.description: The company has processes and procedures in place to capture, log and verify requests, inquires, complaints, or disputes related to the individual's privacy rights of access, review, modification, and/or deletion of personal information. Access requests for personal information are logged within the company's designated tracking system for historical and audit purposes.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: Personal information securely disposed
controls.description: The company securely disposes of personal information in accordance with documented policies and procedures. Personal information is either anonymized, securely erased and/or destroyed when no longer required.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Use, Retention, and Disposal

requirements.title: Data subject access to personal information

controls.title: Identity verification conducted
controls.description: The company, prior to granting an individual the ability to access and review personal information, authenticates the individuals or their authorized representative's identity, with an appropriate level of assurance, and verifies such access is not prohibited by law.

controls.title: Personal information changes communicated
controls.description: The company communicates corrections or erasures of an individual's personal information to authorized users and relevant third parties to whom the personal information has been shared or transferred.

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification
controls.title: Legal personal information tracked
controls.description: The company has personal information that is disclosed for legal purposes logged, tracked, and maintained in the company's designated tracking system for historical and audit purposes.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification
controls.title: Privacy information purpose communicated
controls.description: The company documents new purposes for previously collected information, notifies individuals of the new purpose and use of previously collected information, obtains and records an individual’s consent for use or withdrawal, and ensures consented information is being used in accordance with the documented new purpose.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification
controls.title: Third party privacy documentation reviewed
controls.description: The company has established, maintains, and reviews, at least annually, documentation on the nature, extent, and purpose of personal information collected, processed, stored, and/or disclosed to third parties.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification
controls.title: Private data shared upon request
controls.description: The company provides requested information, after verification, in a timely manner in either a portable electronic format or by mail, in accordance with applicable law.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Disclosure and Notification

controls.title: Personal data update mechanisms available
controls.description: Individuals, customers, or designated account holders can update their personal information to ensure it is accurate and complete through the use of a customer web portal or by contacting the organization using the methods provided in the privacy policy.

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Monitoring and Enforcement
controls.title: Privacy compliant procedures established
controls.description: The company has documented processes and procedures in place to ensure that any privacy-related complaints are addressed, and the resolution is documented in the company's designated tracking system and communicated to the individual.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Monitoring and Enforcement

controls.categoryTitle: Privacy Criteria Related to Monitoring and Enforcement
controls.title: Risk management program established
controls.description: The company has a documented risk management program in place that includes guidance on the identification of potential threats, rating the significance of the risks associated with the identified threats, and mitigation strategies for those risks.
controls.controlGroup: Privacy Criteria Related to Monitoring and Enforcement

tests.title: Company has an approved Risk Management Policy
tests.description: This test verifies that your company has an approved Risk Management Policy in Vanta.

tests.title: Personnel agree to Risk Management Policy
tests.description: Verifies that all relevant personnel have agreed to the Risk Management Policy.

requirements.title: Understanding the organization and its context

controls.title: Understanding the organization and its context
controls.description: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its information security management system.

tests.title: Company has an approved 01-ISMS Scope of the ISMS
tests.description: Verifies that a 01-ISMS Scope of the ISMS has been created and approved within Vanta.

requirements.title: Understanding the needs of interested parties

controls.title: Understanding the needs of interested parties
controls.description: The organization shall determine: a) interested parties that are relevant to the information security management system; b) the relevant requirements of these interested parties; c) which of these requirements will be addressed through the information security management system.

requirements.title: Determining the scope of the information security management system

controls.title: Determining the scope of the information security management system
controls.description: The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the information security management system to establish its scope. When determining this scope, the organization shall consider: a) the external and internal issues referred to in 4.1; b) the requirements referred to in 4.2; c) interfaces and dependencies between activities performed by the organization, and those that are performed by other organizations. The scope shall be available as documented information.

controls.title: Information security management system
controls.description: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve an information security management system, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of ISO . Company has an approved 01-ISMS Scope of the ISMS

tests.title: Company has an approved 02-ISMS Information Security Management System (ISMS) Policy
tests.description: This test checks if your company has an approved 02-ISMS Information Security Management System (ISMS) Policy in place.

controls.title: Leadership and commitment
controls.description: Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the information security management system by: a) ensuring the information security policy and the information security objectives are established and are compatible with the strategic direction of the organization; b) ensuring the integration of the information security management system requirements into the organization’s processes; c) ensuring that the resources needed for the information security management system are available; d) communicating the importance of effective information security management and of conforming to the information security management system requirements; e) ensuring that the information security management system achieves its intended outcome(s); f) directing and supporting persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the information security management system; g) promoting continual improvement; and h) supporting other relevant management roles to demonstrate their leadership as it applies to their areas of responsibility.

tests.title: Company has an approved 03-ISMS Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
tests.description: Verifies that a 03-ISMS Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities has been created and approved within Vanta.

controls.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
controls.description: Top management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated within the organization. Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the information security management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the information security management system to top management.

requirements.title: General actions to address risks and opportunities

controls.title: General actions to address risks and opportunities
controls.description: When planning for the information security management system, the organization shall consider the issues referred to in 4.1 and the requirements referred to in 4.2 and determine the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed to: a) ensure the information security management system can achieve its intended outcome(s); b) prevent, or reduce, undesired effects; c) achieve continual improvement. The organization shall plan: d) actions to address these risks and opportunities; and e) how to integrate and implement the actions into its information security management system processes; and evaluate the effectiveness of these actions

tests.title: Company has an approved 04-ISMS Risk Assessment and Risk Treatment Process
tests.description: Verifies that a 04-ISMS Risk Assessment and Risk Treatment Process has been created and approved within Vanta.

tests.title: Company has an approved 09-ISMS Procedure for Corrective Action and Continual Improvement
tests.description: Verifies that a 09-ISMS Procedure for Corrective Action and Continual Improvement has been created and approved within Vanta.

tests.title: Company has an approved 10-ISMS Information Security Objectives Plan
tests.description: This test verifies whether your company has an approved 10-ISMS Information Security Objectives Plan.

tests.title: Completed risk assessment
tests.description: Completed risk assessment
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of the most recent complete periodic risk assessment, including any associated risk treatment plans. Guidance: Here's a sample template. Google docs template / Excel template Note: This evidence is not required if using Vanta's Risk Module.

controls.title: Information security risk assessment
controls.description: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk assessment process that: a) establishes and maintains information security risk criteria that include: the risk acceptance criteria; and criteria for performing information security risk assessments; b) ensures that repeated information security risk assessments produce consistent, valid and comparable results; c) identifies the information security risks: apply the information security risk assessment process to identify risks associated with the loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability for information within the scope of the information security management system; and identify the risk owners; d) analyses the information security risks: assess the potential consequences that would result if the risks identified in 6.1.2 c) 1) were to materialize; assess the realistic likelihood of the occurrence of the risks identified in 6.1.2 c) 1); and determine the levels of risk; e) evaluates the information security risks: compare the results of risk analysis with the risk criteria established in 6.1.2 a); and prioritize the analysed risks for risk treatment. The organization shall retain documented information about the information security risk assessment process.

controls.title: Information security risk treatment
controls.description: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk treatment process to: a) select appropriate information security risk treatment options, taking account of the risk assessment results; b) determine all controls that are necessary to implement the information security risk treatment option(s) chosen; c) compare the controls determined in 6.1.3 b) above with those in Annex A and verify that no necessary controls have been omitted; d) produce a Statement of Applicability that contains: — the necessary controls (see 6.1.3 b) and c)); — justification for their inclusion; — whether the necessary controls are implemented or not; and — the justification for excluding any of the Annex A controls. e) formulate an information security risk treatment plan; and f) obtain risk owners’ approval of the information security risk treatment plan and acceptance of the residual information security risks. The organization shall retain documented information about the information security risk treatment process.

tests.title: Company has an approved 11-ISMS Statement of Applicability
tests.description: Verifies that a 11-ISMS Statement of Applicability has been created and approved within Vanta.

requirements.title: Information security objective and planning to achieve them

controls.title: Information security objective and planning to achieve them
controls.description: The organization shall establish information security objectives at relevant functions and levels. The information security objectives shall: a) be consistent with the information security policy; b) be measurable (if practicable); c) take into account applicable information security requirements, and results from risk assessment and risk treatment; d) be monitored; e) be communicated; f) be updated as appropriate; g) be available as documented information. The organization shall retain documented information on the information security objectives. When planning how to achieve its information security objectives, the organization shall determine: h) what will be done; i) what resources will be required; j) who will be responsible; k) when it will be completed; and l) how the results will be evaluated.

controls.title: Planning of Changes
controls.description: When the organization determines the need for changes to the information security management system, the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner.

tests.title: Planning changes of the ISMS
tests.description: Planning changes of the ISMS
tests.evidenceGuidance: Evidence that when changes to the ISMS are required (such as significant new procedures, structural changes to the organizations security or operations, or other security risk impacting changes occur) that they are planned and implemented using established change management processes. This can be a project management process example, management review meeting discussion and planning of the change, or change tickets for implementation. The important element is showing that that the ISMS isn't modified in material or significant ways without the risk and impact to its operation from the modification being evaluated and the change is planned and managed according to company policy.

controls.title: Resources
controls.description: The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the information security management system.

controls.title: Competence
controls.description: The organization shall: a) determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its information security performance; b) ensure that these persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, or experience; c) where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken; and d) retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence.

tests.title: Competence is evaluated prior to offer and hiring
tests.description: Competence is evaluated prior to offer and hiring
tests.evidenceGuidance: Evidence or hiring procedure template that shows candidates are formally evaluated for competence in role against expected skill levels during hiring process. A template can be found here: Google docs template

tests.title: ISMS and security program leadership qualifications
tests.description: ISMS and security program leadership qualifications
tests.evidenceGuidance: Evidence such as LinkedIn profiles, resumes, certifications, training or education records demonstrating that ISMS or security program leaders are qualified to have decision-making power over the security program. A template can be found here: Google docs template

controls.title: Awareness
controls.description: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: a) the information security policy; b) their contribution to the effectiveness of the information security management system, including the benefits of improved information security performance; and c) the implications of not conforming with the information security management system requirements.

tests.title: Company has an approved 06-ISMS Information Security Communication Plan
tests.description: Verifies that a 06-ISMS Information Security Communication Plan has been created and approved within Vanta.

tests.title: Security awareness training completion
tests.description: Security awareness training completion
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of recurring security awareness training completion by your employees. Note: Provide this only if you're NOT using Vanta's security awareness training modules. A template can be found here: Google docs template

controls.title: Communication
controls.description: The organization shall determine the need for internal and external communications relevant to the information security management system including: a) on what to communicate; b) when to communicate; c) with whom to communicate; d) how to communicate.

controls.title: Documented information
controls.description: The organization’s information security management system shall include: a) documented information required by this document; and b) documented information determined by the organization as being necessary for the effectiveness of the information security management system.

tests.title: Company has an approved 05-ISMS Procedure for the Control of Documented Information
tests.description: Verifies that a 05-ISMS Procedure for the Control of Documented Information has been created and approved within Vanta.

controls.title: Creating and Updating
controls.description: When creating and updating documented information the organization shall ensure appropriate: a) identification and description (e.g. a title, date, author, or reference number); b) format (e.g. language, software version, graphics) and media (e.g. paper, electronic); and c) review and approval for suitability and adequacy.

controls.title: Control of documented information
controls.description: Documented information required by the information security management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure: a) it is available and suitable for use, where and when it is needed; and b) it is adequately protected (e.g. from loss of confidentiality, improper use, or loss of integrity). For the control of documented information, the organization shall address the following activities, as applicable: c) distribution, access, retrieval and use; d) storage and preservation, including the preservation of legibility; e) control of changes (e.g. version control); and f) retention and disposition. Documented information of external origin, determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the information security management system, shall be identified as appropriate, and controlled.

controls.title: Operation planning and control
controls.description: The organization shall plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements, and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6, by: — establishing criteria for the processes; — implementing control of the processes in accordance with the criteria. Documented information shall be available to the extent necessary to have confidence that the processes have been carried out as planned. The organization shall control planned changes and review the consequences of unintended changes, taking action to mitigate any adverse effects, as necessary. The organization shall ensure that externally provided processes, products or services that are relevant to the information security management system are controlled.

controls.title: Information security risk assessment
controls.description: The organization shall perform information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur, taking account of the criteria established in 6.1.2 a). The organization shall retain documented information of the results of the information security risk assessments.

controls.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation
controls.description: The organization shall determine: a) what needs to be monitored and measured, including information security processes and controls; b) the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, as applicable, to ensure valid results. The methods selected should produce comparable and reproducible results to be considered valid; c) when the monitoring and measuring shall be performed; d) who shall monitor and measure; e) when the results from monitoring and measurement shall be analyzed and evaluated; f) who shall analyze and evaluate these results. Documented information shall be available as evidence of the results. The organization shall evaluate the information security performance and the effectiveness of the information security management system.

controls.title: Internal Audit - General
controls.description: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the information security management system: a) conforms to the organization’s own requirements for its information security management system; the requirements of this document; b) is effectively implemented and maintained.

tests.title: Company has an approved 07-ISMS Procedure for Internal Audits
tests.description: Verifies that a 07-ISMS Procedure for Internal Audits has been created and approved within Vanta.

tests.title: Internal audit report
tests.description: Internal audit report
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of your latest internal audit report. The internal audit must be conducted by an independent person with subject matter expertise in performing internal audits. The person who performs the audit cannot be part of the team that implemented the in-scope audit controls or that has oversight/responsibilities over the results of control performance. The internal auditor can be an internal employee, contractor, or third-party vendor, provided that the independence and expertise criteria are met.

controls.title: Internal Audit Program
controls.description: The organization shall plan, establish, implement and maintain an audit programme(s), including the frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting. When establishing the internal audit programme(s), the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits. The organization shall: a) define the audit criteria and scope for each audit; b) select auditors and conduct audits that ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process; c) ensure that the results of the audits are reported to relevant management; Documented information shall be available as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme(s) and the audit results.

tests.title: Audit Cycle identified
tests.description: Audit Cycle identified
tests.evidenceGuidance: Evidence of Audit Cycle the company undergoes including planned and past assessment dates. This can be done via project management tooling, calendar invites or blocks, or even a simple spreadsheet or document with dates for planned assessments. A template can be found here: Google docs template

controls.title: Management review - General
controls.description: Top management shall review the organization's information security management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

tests.title: Company has an approved 08-ISMS Procedure for Management Review
tests.description: Verifies that a 08-ISMS Procedure for Management Review has been created and approved within Vanta.

tests.title: Management review of ISMS
tests.description: Management review of ISMS
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of your most recent, periodic review of the ISMS by management, as outlined in your management review policy. Guidance: Establish a management review policy and ensure meetings take place on a periodic basis with documentation on the results of the meeting. A template can be found here: Google docs template

controls.title: Management review inputs
controls.description: The management review shall include consideration of: a) the status of actions from previous management reviews; b) changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the information security management system; c) changes in needs and expectations of interested parties that are relevant to the information security management system; d) feedback on the information security performance, including trends in: nonconformities and corrective actions; monitoring and measurement results; audit results; fulfilment of information security objectives; e) feedback from interested parties; f) results of risk assessment and status of risk treatment plan; g) opportunities for continual improvement.

controls.title: Management review results
controls.description: The results of the management review shall include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any needs for changes to the information security management system. Documented information shall be available as evidence of the results of management reviews.

tests.title: Management Review presentation example
tests.description: Management Review presentation example
tests.evidenceGuidance: Please provide an example of a completed Management Review Meeting Presentation. The example should include (at minimum): Previous action follow up Changes to Risk, Security/Threat landscape or other ISMS functions since last meeting ISMS Performance Interested parties feedback Risk management results Continuous improvement

tests.title: Management Review records example
tests.description: Management Review records example
tests.evidenceGuidance: Please provide an example of a Management Review Meeting notes taken during the management review meeting. These notes should accurately reflect discussion and decisions made during the meeting and should include the names of those in attendance and other relevant information.

controls.title: Continual Improvement
controls.description: The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system.

tests.title: Track and address nonconformities
tests.description: Track and address nonconformities
tests.evidenceGuidance: Upload a copy of a nonconformity or continuous improvement tracking sheet used by the organization to evaluate the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system after an issue is identified Guidance: Here's a sample nonconformity tracker (Google docs template / Excel template). Audit Consideration: During your audit window, be prepared to re-upload evidence showing at least 10% of non-conformities identified had root cause analysis created, corrective action outlined, and re-evaluation confirmation, as randomly selected and requested by your auditor.

controls.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
controls.description: When a Nonconformity occurs, the organization shall: a) React to the nonconformity, and as applicable: take action to control and correct it; deal with the consequences b) evaluate the need for action to eliminate the causes of nonconformity, in order that it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by; reviewing the nonconformity; determining the causes of the nonconformity; and determining if similar nonconformities exist, or could potentially occur c) implement any action needed; d) review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken; and e) make changes to the information security management system, if necessary. Corrective actions shall be appropriate to the effects of the nonconformities encountered. Documented information shall be available as evidence of: f) The nature of the nonconformities and any subsequent actions taken, g) the results of any corrective action.

controls.title: Policies for information security
controls.description: Information security policy and topic-specific policies shall be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals and if significant changes occur.

tests.title: Proof of policy availability to employees
tests.description: Proof of policy availability to employees
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence demonstrating that company policies, including the information security policy and topic-specific policies, are accessible to all employees. The evidence should confirm that policies are published in a centralized location, easily reachable, and consistently maintained for employee access. Acceptable Evidence Includes: Screenshots of the internal wiki or documentation portal (e.g., Confluence, SharePoint, Google Drive, intranet site) showing where policies are stored. A table of contents or directory listing available policies. Access control settings confirming that all employees have read permissions. Screenshots of internal announcements (e.g., email, Slack, Teams messages) informing employees where policies are located. Screenshots of onboarding materials that direct new employees to the policy repository. Records of employee acknowledgments confirming they have accessed and reviewed policies. Note: If this is handled within Vanta, simply "Add URL" to the onboarding page. Audit Consideration: During your audit window, be prepared to re-upload evidence for at least a 10% of your employees, contractors and applicable third party users to confirm they can access these policies, as randomly selected and requested by your auditor.

controls.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Information security roles and responsibilities shall be defined and allocated according to the organization needs.

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.description: Conflicting duties and conflicting areas of responsibility shall be segregated.

controls.title: Security association membership
controls.description: Provide proof of membership in at least one recognized security association, e.g., ISACA, AITP, ITIL, by at least one Information Security team member.

controls.title: Security newsletter / group subscription
controls.description: Provide screenshots of emails from two different security-related subscriptions received by Information Security team members. Examples: Krebs on Security, NIST, US Cert, CISA, Security-focused Slack channels.

controls.title: Threat Intelligence
controls.description: Information relating to information security threats shall be collected and analyzed to produce threat intelligence.

tests.title: A process exists to identify and prioritize security vulnerabilities
tests.description: A process exists to identify and prioritize security vulnerabilities
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide documentation outlining the process for identifying, tracking, and remediating vulnerabilities using external threat intelligence sources. Acceptable evidence can include: A procedural document describing how vulnerability scan results are reviewed and incorporated into threat analysis. Evidence that external sources (e.g., vendor alerts, RSS feeds, security bulletins) are monitored for emerging threats. Examples of how vulnerabilities are prioritized and remediated, such as ticketing workflows or remediation reports.

tests.title: Operational alert dashboard
tests.description: Operational alert dashboard
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot from your application monitoring dashboard, such as from Datadog or New Relic, showing alert configurations.

tests.title: Intrusion detection system alerts
tests.description: Intrusion detection system alerts
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that your Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and/or Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) are set up to detect and alert when unusual or potentially harmful activity occurs on your network or systems. Acceptable evidence can include: screenshot or copy of an alert email, dashboard notification, or system log (e.g., multiple failed login attempts, unexpected network traffic, or a malware detection). screenshot of your security tool’s settings confirming that alerts are turned on and actively monitoring for threats. (A firewall rule in Palo Alto, Cisco, or Fortinet that triggers an alert when suspicious traffic is detected.) report or system log showing historical alerts and actions taken (e.g., a log from an EDR tool like SentinelOne or a SIEM system like Splunk or Datadog).

Retrieve the visitor log records for the last 30 days. Ensure the log includes details such as visitor names, dates, times, and purpose of visits. tests.title: Planned access review
tests.description: Planned access review
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a ticket or calendar invite demonstrating that a periodic access review was planned and completed. Guidance: For additional information on how to fulfill this evidence request, see this guiding document: Google docs template / Docx template. Note: Current access data can be exported from the Access page Implementation guidance Determine how often access reviews should occur (e.g., quarterly for critical systems, semi-annually for business tools). List the systems, roles, or departments that must be reviewed on a recurring basis. Create a calendar event or ticket in your task/project management system for each planned access review. Include reviewers, systems in scope, and a link to your access export or review template. Keep a centralized tracker or calendar of all planned access reviews, with fields for date, system, reviewer, and status. This helps ensure accountability and makes it easy to produce evidence during audits. Evidence collection To collect evidence for planned access reviews, focus on submitting documentation that proves the review was intentionally scheduled as part of a recurring access governance process. Provide a calendar invite, ticket, or task assignment that includes the date of the review, systems or departments in scope, and assigned reviewers. Confirm that the artifact clearly states the review’s objective (e.g., “Q3 Infrastructure Access Review” or “HR System Entitlement Review”). Include attachments or links, if available, to supporting documentation such as the access export or review checklist. Ensure that the scheduling or planning record is time-stamped and tied to a recurring cadence (e.g., quarterly, semi-annually). If applicable, submit screenshots from project management tools (e.g., Jira, Asana, Notion) that show the task status and assignee. Note: Current access data can be exported from the Access page

tests.title: Privileged user lists generated
tests.description: Privileged user lists generated
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot or system export showing the administrative users for all in-scope systems and applications. You should consider users of all types, including business partners, service accounts, vendor and third party accounts, contractors, and employees. Guidance: Typical in-scope systems include: Background checkers Cloud providers Communication platforms CRM platforms Database/Data warehouse providers Endpoint security tools HRIS Identity providers MDM tools Vulnerability scanners SIEM tools Version control systems DevOps tools Document repositories Guidance: Ensure that the privileged access configured for your in-scope systems is based on active and current roles & responsibilities of those assigned individuals. If there are newly added individuals, ensure that you followed your access provisioning process to create / modify the accounts, and removed any personnel that did not require the access anymore. Audit Consideration: During your audit window, be prepared to re-upload evidence for at least a 10% of your privileged user accounts, as randomly selected and requested by your auditor. Note: This evidence is only required for admin users of tools that have not been connected to Vanta via the integrations page. For tools that have been integrated into Vanta, no additional evidence is needed for this document. A template can be found here: Google docs template Implementation guidance Identify and inventory systems not integrated with Vanta. Engage system owners and administrators to obtain or generate current reports of administrative users, ensuring the list captures business partners, service accounts, vendors, third-party accounts, contractors, and employees. Establish a routine process for updating these lists by defining clear responsibilities and review cycles, documenting role changes and verifying the removal of unnecessary access. Consolidate the updated lists and supporting documentation into an accessible evidence package, and schedule periodic reviews to ensure ongoing accuracy and compliance. Evidence collection To collect evidence for the control of maintaining privileged user lists, you would typically gather documentation that reflects current access roles and responsibilities. Request a current list or report of administrative users from system administrators. Verify that the list includes all relevant user types, such as business partners, service accounts, vendors, third-party accounts, contractors, and employees. Ensure the list is updated to reflect any changes in roles or access, removing unnecessary access. Confirm that the list is only for systems not integrated with Vanta.

tests.title: Customer account access request
tests.description: Customer account access request
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide an example of a recent access request and approval flow, such as through a Jira ticket or email, to grant employee access to customer data in your application. Guidance: Best practice is to track and document data access requests through tickets or utilization of an identity access management tool (IAM). However, if tickets or a data access management tool is not being used, email threads and/or a manual access request form may also be acceptable. Here's a sample access request form: Google docs template / Docx template. Implementation guidance Set up a secure customer submission process using a support ticket system, web form, or dedicated email channel that logs each request with details like date, customer identifier (sanitized), and request type. Develop and implement an internal process where each request is validated (e.g., verifying identity through multi-factor checks), tracked, approved by a designated support agent or team, and followed by record-keeping of actions taken. Create or update standard operating procedures (SOPs) and checklists that outline each step of the process, ensuring that all evidence—including submission timestamps and resolution details—is stored in an auditable, secure repository. Evidence collection To collect evidence of customer account access request handling, provide records that demonstrate secure, traceable, and consistent processes. Submit a support ticket, form submission, or email request from a customer requesting account access or changes (e.g., password reset, account ownership transfer). Include internal handling records showing how the request was validated and fulfilled (e.g., verification steps, approval, response). Ensure the evidence shows the date, requester, responsible support agent or team, and resolution outcome. Provide documentation of any standard operating procedures (SOPs) or checklists used to manage such requests securely. Sanitize any personal data in the submission before sharing evidence.

tests.title: Version control system access review
tests.description: Version control system access review
tests.evidenceGuidance: Please provide evidence of the last access review performed on your version control system(s). Implementation guidance Configure your version control system to generate and store detailed activity logs that include user access rights, modifications, and review dates. If native logging isn’t enough, explore integrations or simple scripts to capture these events automatically. Establish a periodic review process where a designated team member verifies the logs, ensuring all access rights and changes are documented. This process should culminate in a formal review report that aligns with your organization’s access control policies. Document the review process—including roles, steps taken, and evidence collected—and securely archive the reports. This documentation not only aids in demonstrating compliance but also supports ongoing process improvements. Evidence collection To collect evidence for the access review of a version control system, gather documentation that details user access rights, any changes made, and the date of the review. Obtain the most recent access review report or log file from the version control system. Ensure the document includes a list of users with access, their access levels, and any modifications to access rights. Verify that the document is dated and reflects the latest review conducted. Confirm that the report aligns with the organization's access control policies.

tests.description: Autoscaling
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that Autoscaling is enabled where appropriate or where pre-approved autoscaling requests are accepted and documented as pre-approved in the SDLC. Guidance: Azure Autoscaling guidance AWS Autoscaling guidance GCP Autoscaling guidance Implementation guidance Enable autoscaling in your environment using the appropriate cloud service (e.g., AWS Auto Scaling, Azure Scale Sets, or GCP Autoscaler) and set thresholds to trigger scaling events. Document autoscaling configuration decisions and pre-approvals in your SDLC artifacts—this might include architecture diagrams, infrastructure-as-code files, and change request tickets. Capture autoscaling logs, dashboards, or approval documentation and retain them in a centralized location for compliance verification. Evidence collection To collect this evidence, gather technical and process documentation demonstrating that autoscaling is either implemented or formally pre-approved within the organization’s cloud environments. Retrieve configuration settings or screenshots from your cloud environment (AWS, Azure, GCP) confirming autoscaling is active. Export logs or reports from your autoscaling service that show thresholds, usage patterns, or trigger events. tests.title: Capacity monitoring dashboard
tests.description: Capacity monitoring dashboard
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot from your capacity monitoring dashboards (e.g., Datadog, New Relic) showing current status, assets being monitored, and relevant metrics. Customize your dashboard to clearly display real-time capacity status, key performance indicators, and the list of monitored assets. Navigate to a dashboard displaying system performance metrics (CPU, memory, disk, etc.), infrastructure assets being monitored, and current operational status. tests.title: Secure configuration baselines developed
tests.description: Secure configuration baselines developed
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of documented configuration baselines based on industry standards such as CIS, NIST 800 series, NIST STIGs, etc.) for all in-scope systems such as: Operating Systems Cloud Infrastructure and Services Servers or Compute Instances Endpoint Software Network Infrastructure (Firewalls, VPCs, Security Groups) Databases Acceptable evidence can include: A configuration baseline document outlining security settings for each in-scope system. Screenshots or reports from security tools (e.g., CIS Benchmark scans, AWS Security Hub findings) showing compliance with baseline standards. Documentation of access controls, logging configurations, and system monitoring settings. A simple spreadsheet listing key configurations and security settings applied across systems. Implementation Guidance for Startups: If you don’t have a mature IT team, start with these steps: Identify what you use – List the technologies you rely on (e.g., AWS, Linux, Windows, databases, firewalls). Use existing templates – Download CIS benchmarks or NIST STIGs relevant to your technology stack. Many security tools (e.g., AWS Security Hub, Microsoft Defender) provide default recommendations. Apply basic hardening – Disable unnecessary services, enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA), enable logging, and restrict admin access. Document in a simple format – A Google Doc or spreadsheet listing key security settings is enough to start. Track what’s configured, who owns it, and when it was last reviewed. Set up alerts & reviews – Use built-in cloud security tools (AWS Config, Azure Security Center) to monitor compliance, and schedule periodic checks (quarterly or biannually) to keep settings up to date. Audit Consideration: During your audit window, be prepared to re-upload evidence for at least a 10% for your interconnected system components, as randomly selected and requested by your auditor. A template can be found here: Google docs template Implementation guidance Identify all in-scope systems and any existing configuration documentation. Determine where security settings, access controls, and logging configurations need to be defined according to industry standards. Create or update configuration baseline documents for each system. Use industry guidelines (e.g., CIS, NIST 800 series, NIST STIGs) to outline secure settings and ensure documentation covers operating systems, cloud infrastructure, servers, endpoints, networks, and databases. Use security tools to regularly scan and assess configurations. Collect and archive tool reports and audit logs that demonstrate compliance, making sure all evidence is current and accessible. Evidence collection To collect this evidence, gather documents and reports showing secure configuration standards. Obtain baseline documents listing secure settings by system type. Collect screenshots or reports from security tools (e.g., AWS Security Hub, CIS scans). Document logging, access control, and system hardening settings. Compile a spreadsheet or simple report tracking what is applied, to what systems, and who owns it. Ensure all evidence is current and reflects actual system configurations.
