tests.description: Customer data deletion record
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot or piece of evidence (e.g., completed ticket in Jira or Linear) demonstrating that customer data is deleted when a Data Deletion Request is formally requested, in accordance with your defined SLA. The Data Privacy Policy at your organization should include details on their data rights, categories of data collected about them, and the process to formally file a Data Deletion Request. If there have been no customer data deletion requests, you may upload evidence including your Privacy Policy and the mechanism to request deletion or a detailed, internal procedural document. Note: This is only applicable if you've had a deletion request and successfully fulfilled it in the past 12 months. Useful links: [GDPR's Right to Erasure](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-17-gdpr/ / CCPA's Right to Delete.) Implementation guidance Define how customers can submit data deletion requests—typically through a privacy request form, email, or support channel. Assign ownership to a designated team (e.g., privacy, support, or legal) for handling and fulfilling these requests. Maintain a secure, access-controlled record of all deletion requests. For each entry, include: Date of request, requestor’s identity or account reference, systems or data types affected, date of completion, request handler or owner, and confirmation of deletion or system-specific outcome. Ensure that appropriate teams validate the data has been deleted from all relevant systems (production, backups, third-party services if applicable). Optionally, send a confirmation message to the customer and store a copy in the record. Evidence collection To collect evidence for a customer data deletion control, you would gather documentation showing compliance with data deletion requests. This involves ensuring that requests are processed according to your Data Privacy Policy and Service Level Agreement (SLA). Obtain a screenshot or completed ticket from a system like Jira or Linear that documents the data deletion request and its resolution. If no requests have been made, provide your Data Privacy Policy and the procedure for requesting data deletion. Ensure the documentation includes timestamps, request details, and confirmation of data deletion.

tests.title: Data auto-deleted when retention period expires
tests.description: Data auto-deleted when retention period expires
tests.evidenceGuidance: Evidence that data is automatically deleted when its retention period is reached Implementation guidance Define and document your data retention rules: Clearly outline retention periods for each data type, update your data retention policies, and ensure these guidelines are approved by relevant stakeholders. Configure automated deletion in your system: Work with your IT team to set up scheduled tasks or scripts that trigger the removal of expired data, ensuring the system logs these deletion activities for future evidence. Validate and monitor the process: Test the automated deletion mechanism, review system logs or reports regularly, and adjust configurations as needed to confirm consistent compliance with your data retention policy. Evidence collection To collect evidence that data is automatically deleted once its retention period expires, focus on obtaining system-generated reports or logs that demonstrate this process. Review system logs or audit trails that show data deletion activities. Obtain reports from the data management system confirming the deletion of expired data. Gather documentation of data retention policies and procedures to verify alignment with system operations. Request screenshots or records of system configurations that enforce data retention rules.

controls.title: Data masking
controls.description: Data masking shall be used in accordance with the organization’s topic-specific policy on access control and other related topic-specific policies, and business requirements, taking applicable legislation into consideration.

tests.title: Data Masking
tests.description: Data Masking
tests.evidenceGuidance: NOTE: This control is optional if Data Masking is not in scope for your audit. Provide evidence demonstrating that data masking is implemented to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access. The evidence should confirm that masking techniques are in place for both structured and unstructured data, in adherence with policy requirements. Acceptable evidences can include: Screenshots or configuration settings from data masking tools (e.g., Oracle Data Masking, IBM Guardium, Informatica, or custom scripts). Logs or reports from databases showing masked values in non-production environments. Screenshots of masked data within applications, reports, or logs demonstrating that sensitive data is obfuscated. Role-based access control (RBAC) settings demonstrating that only authorized users can access unmasked data. Logs showing access attempts and enforcement of data masking rules. Results of data masking effectiveness tests, including screenshots or sample queries showing masked versus unmasked data. Implementation guidance Identify and classify sensitive data across structured and unstructured sources, then select a data masking tool or solution that aligns with your policy requirements. Configure the tool by setting up masking rules for the identified data fields, ensuring these rules apply consistently across data formats, and integrate role-based access controls. Validate and document the implementation by capturing screenshots or exporting configuration settings, generating logs that display masked values, and reviewing access controls for authorized users only. Evidence collection To collect evidence of data masking: Gather configuration settings from your masking tools or scripts that apply masking rules to sensitive fields. Capture logs or screenshots showing masked values in staging or analytics environments. Obtain RBAC settings that enforce masking visibility. Export sample test results showing masking was applied and validated.

controls.title: Data leakage prevention
controls.description: Data leakage prevention measures shall be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.

controls.title: Information backup
controls.description: Backup copies of information, software and systems shall be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.

tests.title: Data restore test
tests.description: Data restore test
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence demonstrating that periodic database recovery or restore tests are planned and completed successfully from backups.Acceptable evidence and implementation guidance: Documented Test Plans and Schedules: Outline the frequency and scope of planned database recovery tests. Regular testing ensures that backups can be restored effectively in case of data loss or system failure. Test Execution Records: Maintain records of executed recovery tests, including dates, personnel involved, and outcomes. This documentation demonstrates adherence to the backup policy and the effectiveness of recovery procedures. Validation Reports: After each recovery test, compile reports detailing the validation of post-recovery results, identification of any errors or issues, and corrective actions taken. Regular testing of backup jobs is essential to ensure data availability and to measure recovery times against organizational objectives. Implementation guidance Define and document the backup and restore test plan: Establish clear procedures outlining the frequency, scope, and specific steps for performing data restore tests. Include details like responsible personnel, roles, and a schedule for testing. Execute the restore tests per the plan, keeping detailed records of each test session—including steps taken, issues encountered, and resolutions. Ensure these records capture all relevant data for validation. After each test, generate test results/validation reports confirming that the restore procedures met backup policies and were successful. Use these reports to refine processes and schedule future tests. Evidence collection To collect evidence for the control related to data restore tests, focus on documentation that demonstrates the planning and execution of these tests. Evidence should include test plans, schedules, execution records, and test results/validation reports. Gather test plans and schedules that outline the frequency and scope of restore tests. Collect execution records that detail the steps taken during the tests and any issues encountered. Obtain test results/validation reports that confirm the success of the tests and adherence to backup policies. Ensure documentation is up-to-date and reflects recent test activities.

tests.title: Backups completed for other databases
tests.description: Backups completed for other databases
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that backup copies of information, software, and systems are properly configured and maintained for any in-scope system not covered by an automated backup test in Vanta. Acceptable evidences can include: Screenshot or export showing the backup settings for the system, including frequency, retention period, and storage location. Evidence that backups are enabled and running as scheduled. Logs or reports confirming successful backup completions over time. Screenshots or records proving restoration tests have been performed to confirm that backups are functional. Documentation showing the date, scope, and results of the latest restoration test. If using a third-party or cloud backup service (e.g., AWS Backup, Veeam, Acronis), provide configuration details or reports. Implementation guidance Identify and configure your backup system for each in-scope database by setting up regular backup schedules and ensuring backup settings (e.g., retention policies, versioning) are captured in the management console. Enable logging for all backup activities so that each successful backup run generates a log entry or report; periodically perform restoration tests and document the results. Collect and store evidence such as screenshots or exported configuration files, log excerpts, and test restoration documentation in a centralized repository to demonstrate ongoing compliance. Evidence collection To collect evidence for the control related to backups of databases, focus on gathering technical evidence that demonstrates proper configuration and maintenance of backup systems. Access the backup management console or system to capture screenshots or export settings that show backup configurations. Retrieve logs that confirm successful completion of backups. Document results from restoration tests to verify backup integrity. If third-party services are used, obtain configuration details or reports from the service provider.

controls.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
controls.description: Information processing facilities shall be implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements.

tests.title: RDS Multi-AZ deployment configured (AWS)
tests.description: This test verifies that AWS RDS database instances are configured for high availability using Multi-AZ deployment to ensure disaster recovery readiness.

tests.title: Redundant backup or system locations in use
tests.description: Redundant backup or system locations in use
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that backups and systems have acceptable redundancy either via different availability zones, replication or copies, or other methods. Acceptable evidence can include: Evidence/screenshots from cloud management consoles or system configuration files that display settings for multi-zone deployment, replication configurations, or automated backup schedules. Logs or dashboard screenshots from monitoring tools that confirm the operational status of redundant systems and verify that data replication and backup processes are active. System-generated logs that detail routine backup operations and replication events, ensuring that these processes occur as scheduled. Implementation guidance Identify and select a cloud provider or backup solution that supports multi-zone or multi-location deployment. Configure your backup settings to duplicate data across at least two different zones or regions to ensure redundancy. Implement replication processes or scheduled backup jobs using your system’s management tools. Enable logging features to record backup and replication events, ensuring you can later retrieve system-generated logs as evidence. Validate the configuration by reviewing your cloud management console and monitoring tool logs. Capture screenshots and save logs that demonstrate active redundancy—this will help you continuously monitor and prove the control is in place. Evidence collection To collect evidence for redundancy in backup or system locations, focus on gathering technical evidence from system logs and cloud management consoles. Access the cloud management console to capture screenshots showing multi-zone deployment settings. Retrieve logs from monitoring tools that confirm active redundancy processes. Obtain system-generated logs detailing routine backup and replication events.

controls.title: Logging
controls.description: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analysed.

tests.title: Operational alert dashboard
tests.description: Operational alert dashboard
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot from your application monitoring dashboard, such as from Datadog or New Relic, showing alert configurations.

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.description: Networks, systems and applications shall be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.

tests.title: Operational alert dashboard (1)
tests.description: Operational alert dashboard (1)
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide a screenshot from your application monitoring dashboard, such as from Datadog or New Relic, showing alert configurations.

controls.title: Clock synchronization
controls.description: The clocks of information processing systems used by the organization shall be synchronized to approved time sources.

tests.title: Clocks on infrastructure system synchronized
tests.description: This feature is built into AWS.

controls.title: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.description: The use of utility programs that can be capable of overriding system and application controls shall be restricted and tightly controlled.

tests.title: Administrative account non-repudiation
tests.description: Administrative account non-repudiation
tests.evidenceGuidance: Screenshot or other evidence that any use of administrative accounts can be associated with an individual user or employee Note: In situations where administrator accounts must be shared, additional logging or account control mechanisms must be in place to satisfy this control. Implementation guidance Enable logging on all systems where administrative activities occur, ensuring that logs capture user identity, action type, and timestamp for each event. For systems using shared accounts, implement compensating controls such as mandatory session logging, multi-factor authentication, or jump hosts that tie sessions to authenticated users. Review logs regularly and retain them in a central log aggregation system. Periodically test traceability by sampling log entries and confirming user attribution. Evidence collection To collect evidence demonstrating that all administrative account activities can be traced back to individual users, focus on gathering logs and documentation that show user-specific access and actions. Review system logs to identify entries related to administrative account activities. Capture screenshots of logs showing timestamps, user IDs, and actions performed. Ensure that logs include details of shared account usage, with additional logging or control mechanisms in place. Compile documentation that outlines the procedures for logging and monitoring administrative account activities.

tests.title: Change management procedure documentation
tests.description: Change management procedure documentation
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that changes to information processing facilities and information systems are managed according to established change management procedures.Acceptable evidence can include: -A documented change management policy outlining procedures for requesting, assessing, approving, implementing, and reviewing changes.-Records of recent change requests and approvals, demonstrating segregation of duties.-Minutes from Change Advisory Board (CAB) meetings where proposed changes were discussed and approved.-Evidence of impact assessments conducted prior to implementing changes, such as risk assessment reports or testing plans.-Documentation showing that operating procedures and user guidelines are reviewed and updated following changes.-Records indicating that business continuity and disaster recovery plans are evaluated and updated to accommodate changes.A template can be found here: Google docs template Implementation guidance Define and document your change management process by creating or formalizing a procedure, standardized templates, and record-keeping procedures to capture change requests, approvals, meeting minutes, impact assessments, and updates to operating procedures, business continuity, and disaster recovery plans. Establish a centralized repository for storing these documents, ensuring that all relevant stakeholders know where and how to upload and retrieve evidence related to change management activities. Set up regular reviews (e.g., periodic CAB meetings and impact assessments) to update records and verify that all procedural changes are reflected in related plans; this ongoing practice will help ensure continuous compliance and evidence collection for audits. Evidence collection Collect evidence by gathering documentation that demonstrates adherence to change management procedures for information processing facilities and systems. Obtain documented change management procedure. Collect records of recent change requests and approvals. Gather minutes from Change Advisory Board (CAB) meetings. Acquire impact assessments conducted prior to implementing changes, such as risk assessment reports or testing plans. Ensure updated operating procedures are reviewed and updated following changes. Verify that business continuity and disaster recovery plans are reviewed and updated to reflect changes.

requirements.title: Installation of software on operational systems

controls.title: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.description: Procedures and measures shall be implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems.

tests.title: Installed applications monitored
tests.description: Installed applications monitored
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence demonstrating that the organization monitors and controls applications installed by users to prevent unauthorized or non-compliant software usage. This applies to both corporate-managed devices and, where applicable, Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) environments. Acceptable evidence can include: Screenshots of Mobile Device Management (MDM) configurations (e.g., Intune, JAMF, Workspace ONE) enforcing application restrictions. Policies showing whitelisting or blacklisting of applications via Active Directory (AD), Group Policy, or Azure Modern Management. Endpoint protection settings that detect and block unauthorized software. Logs or reports from security tools (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) showing application activity and enforcement actions. Alerts or notifications triggered when unapproved applications are installed. Records of enforcement actions, such as blocked application attempts or incident reports related to unauthorized software. BYOD-Specific Controls (if applicable): Conditional access policies that limit corporate data access based on device compliance status. Screenshots of containerization solutions (e.g., Microsoft Endpoint Manager, VMware Workspace ONE) separating corporate and personal applications. Implementation guidance Establish clear policies: Define acceptable applications, and create whitelisting/blacklisting policies that apply to both corporate devices and BYOD. Document these policies so users and administrators understand what software is allowed. Leverage existing management tools: Configure your Mobile Device Management (MDM) and endpoint protection systems to enforce these application policies. Adjust settings to automatically block unauthorized installations and log all changes related to installed applications. Set up continuous monitoring and documentation: Enable logging within your security tools to track application installations and any enforcement actions taken. Regularly review these logs and configurations to generate evidence that supports ongoing compliance and control over installed applications. Evidence collection To collect evidence for monitoring and controlling installed applications, focus on gathering technical evidence from systems and configurations. Evidence can be collected by reviewing and documenting the configurations and logs of relevant security tools and management systems. Review Mobile Device Management (MDM) configurations to ensure they enforce application policies. Document application whitelisting/blacklisting policies and verify their implementation. Collect logs from endpoint protection tools that monitor application installations. Gather records of enforcement actions taken against unauthorized software installations.

controls.title: Networks security
controls.description: Networks and network devices shall be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

tests.title: EC2 instance public ports restricted (AWS)
tests.description: This test verifies that AWS EC2 instances do not have any unapproved TCP/UDP ports exposed publicly through their security groups. Instances should only expose explicitly permitted ports defined in your configuration.

controls.title: Security of network services
controls.description: Security mechanisms, service levels and service requirements of network services shall be identified, implemented and monitored.

controls.title: Segregation of networks
controls.description: Groups of information services, users and information systems shall be segregated in the organization’s networks.

controls.title: Web filtering
controls.description: Access to external websites shall be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.

tests.title: Web Filtering Capabilities
tests.description: Web Filtering Capabilities
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that demonstrates that your organization has implemented web filtering controls to reduce the risk of personnel accessing websites that contain illegal content, viruses, or phishing materials. This includes blocking access to known or suspected malicious websites, command and control servers, and websites sharing illegal content. Where to find the web filtering evidence: Web Protection in Anti-malware Solutions: Many small businesses already use anti-malware or antivirus software that includes basic web filtering features. If the company has an Anti-malware Solution, it likely has built-in Web Protection or Web Filtering. Where to check: Open the anti-malware software dashboard. Look for sections like Web Protection, Safe Browsing, or Web Control. This will typically list blocked websites or threats encountered during browsing. Capture screenshots of the enabled web filtering settings or download a report from the software. 2) Firewall or Router Settings: If the company uses a business-grade firewall or router (e.g., Cisco, SonicWall, or even certain Netgear routers), web filtering can often be configured directly within these devices. Where to check: Access the firewall or router’s admin panel. Look for sections like URL Filtering, Content Filtering, or Web Filtering. Capture screenshots of the settings and any activity logs showing blocked website attempts. 3) Browser-Based Protections: Modern browsers (like Chrome, Firefox, and Edge) come with built-in protection against dangerous websites. Where to check: In Chrome, go to Settings > Privacy and Security > Security. Check for “Safe Browsing” settings. Capture screenshots of this setting enabled. Implementation guidance Configure a web filtering control on your existing infrastructure (firewall, router, or anti-malware solution) by setting rules to block known malicious domains and content; document all settings and policy details. Test the implementation by accessing known test URLs (or safe simulated environments) to confirm the control's effectiveness, capturing screenshots of alerts or logs showing blocks. Set up automated logging and regular report generation from the filtering tools, then compile periodic evidence (screenshots, configuration exports, and maintenance records) to continuously demonstrate your security posture. Evidence collection To collect evidence for web filtering controls, focus on gathering technical evidence that demonstrates the effectiveness of these controls in blocking malicious websites and content. Capture screenshots of anti-malware solution dashboards showing blocked threats. Document firewall or router settings that specify web filtering rules. Obtain logs or reports from browser-based protection tools indicating blocked access to harmful sites. Compile records of regular updates and maintenance of web filtering systems.

controls.title: Application security requirements
controls.description: Information security requirements shall be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.

requirements.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.description: Principles for engineering secure systems shall be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activities. Company has an approved Secure Development Policy Company has an approved Third-Party Management Policy

tests.title: Secure configuration baselines developed
tests.description: Secure configuration baselines developed
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence of documented configuration baselines based on industry standards such as CIS, NIST 800 series, NIST STIGs, etc.) for all in-scope systems such as: Operating Systems Cloud Infrastructure and Services Servers or Compute Instances Endpoint Software Network Infrastructure (Firewalls, VPCs, Security Groups) Databases Acceptable evidence can include: A configuration baseline document outlining security settings for each in-scope system. Screenshots or reports from security tools (e.g., CIS Benchmark scans, AWS Security Hub findings) showing compliance with baseline standards. Documentation of access controls, logging configurations, and system monitoring settings. A simple spreadsheet listing key configurations and security settings applied across systems. Implementation Guidance for Startups: If you don’t have a mature IT team, start with these steps: Identify what you use – List the technologies you rely on (e.g., AWS, Linux, Windows, databases, firewalls). Use existing templates – Download CIS benchmarks or NIST STIGs relevant to your technology stack. Many security tools (e.g., AWS Security Hub, Microsoft Defender) provide default recommendations. Apply basic hardening – Disable unnecessary services, enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA), enable logging, and restrict admin access. Document in a simple format – A Google Doc or spreadsheet listing key security settings is enough to start. Track what’s configured, who owns it, and when it was last reviewed. Set up alerts & reviews – Use built-in cloud security tools (AWS Config, Azure Security Center) to monitor compliance, and schedule periodic checks (quarterly or biannually) to keep settings up to date. Audit Consideration: During your audit window, be prepared to re-upload evidence for at least a 10% for your interconnected system components, as randomly selected and requested by your auditor. A template can be found here: Google docs template Implementation guidance Identify all in-scope systems and any existing configuration documentation. Determine where security settings, access controls, and logging configurations need to be defined according to industry standards. Create or update configuration baseline documents for each system. Use industry guidelines (e.g., CIS, NIST 800 series, NIST STIGs) to outline secure settings and ensure documentation covers operating systems, cloud infrastructure, servers, endpoints, networks, and databases. Use security tools to regularly scan and assess configurations. Collect and archive tool reports and audit logs that demonstrate compliance, making sure all evidence is current and accessible. Evidence collection To collect this evidence, gather documents and reports showing secure configuration standards. Obtain baseline documents listing secure settings by system type. Collect screenshots or reports from security tools (e.g., AWS Security Hub, CIS scans). Document logging, access control, and system hardening settings. Compile a spreadsheet or simple report tracking what is applied, to what systems, and who owns it. Ensure all evidence is current and reflects actual system configurations.

tests.title: Secure engineering principles defined
tests.description: Secure engineering principles defined
tests.evidenceGuidance: Please upload a completed copy of a Secure Engineering Principles & Planning document. This document should speak to what your organization considers its guiding principles for secure engineering and operate as a north star reference when considering engineering challenges. For ideas on what to consider it is recommended that you review NIST SP 800-160v1r1 also known as "Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems" from NIST. A template can be found here: Google docs template Implementation guidance Collaborate with engineering, product, and security teams to outline your guiding principles. Reference controls and lifecycle practices from NIST SP 800-160v1r1 or similar standards. Create a practical guide that applies each principle across phases like architecture design, threat modeling, dependency management, secure coding, peer review, and release. Approve the Secure Engineering Principles & Planning document through your change management or security governance process. Review it annually or when major architectural changes occur. Communicate and train engineers on how to apply the principles in their day-to-day work. Evidence collection To collect evidence for this control, gather a finalized document that clearly outlines the organization's secure engineering principles and planning methodology: Obtain the Secure Engineering Principles & Planning document. Verify it includes a formal statement of secure design principles (e.g., least privilege, fail securely, threat modeling, defense in depth); design process alignment with standards such as NIST SP 800-160 or ISO 27034; defined roles and responsibilities across engineering and security teams; and integration with your SDLC, DevOps, and CI/CD workflows. Confirm the document has been reviewed and approved by engineering leadership or designated security governance personnel. Ensure the content reflects current organizational practices and technologies and is version-controlled for traceability.

controls.title: Secure coding
controls.description: Secure coding principles shall be applied to software development. Company has an approved Secure Development Policy Company has an approved Third-Party Management Policy

requirements.title: Security testing in development and acceptance

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.description: Security testing processes shall be defined and implemented in the development life cycle.

tests.title: QA process documentation
tests.description: QA process documentation
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide documentation for your formalized QA process. Guidance: Here's a sample QA process. Google docs template / Docx template Implementation guidance Document how code moves from development to production, highlighting the specific QA steps (e.g., automated test suites, staging environment checks, manual testing, release approval). Use simple diagrams or checklists for clarity. Clearly identify who is responsible for writing, reviewing, and approving QA results—this may include developers, QA engineers, or product managers. Store the QA process doc in a shared, version-controlled location (e.g., Confluence, Notion, internal wiki). Review and update it periodically as your development lifecycle evolves. Evidence collection To collect evidence for QA processes, submit documentation that reflects how testing and validation are integrated into your software development lifecycle. Provide a QA policy, procedure, or workflow document that outlines how software is tested before release, including unit tests, integration tests, automated checks, and/or manual QA steps. Include descriptions of approval gates or sign-offs required before deployment (e.g., peer review, QA engineer validation). If using CI/CD pipelines, provide screenshots or excerpts showing test stages integrated into build workflows (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CircleCI). Submit test coverage reports, checklists, or templates used for regression or user acceptance testing (UAT), if applicable. Ensure documents are dated, version-controlled, and reflect current QA practices.

tests.title: QA and acceptance testing
tests.description: QA and acceptance testing
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence that an approved change has successfully undergone acceptance testing before deployment. This should include security test results demonstrating that functional, performance, and security requirements were met. Security testing should cover common vulnerabilities such as those outlined in the OWASP Top 10, as well as any organization-specific security controls, compliance requirements, and risk mitigation measures. Implementation guidance Develop a documented acceptance testing plan that integrates functional, performance, and security tests, ensuring that requirements address common vulnerabilities (like those from the OWASP Top 10) and include organization-specific security controls and compliance standards. Execute the plan and collect detailed test evidence (e.g., logs, screenshots, assessment reports) that clearly shows the test results and any remediation steps taken to address vulnerabilities. Arrange a final review session with relevant stakeholders to verify, approve, and formally sign off the evidence before deployment. Evidence collection Evidence for this control would be collected through documentation and reports related to acceptance testing and security assessments. Review the acceptance testing report to ensure it includes results for functional, performance, and security requirements. Verify that the report addresses common vulnerabilities, such as those in the OWASP Top 10. Confirm that the report includes any organization-specific security controls and compliance requirements. Ensure the report is approved by relevant stakeholders before deployment.

tests.title: Security integration tests
tests.description: Security integration tests
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide evidence demonstrating the implementation of automated security testing within your application or infrastructure, including Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).Acceptable evidence and implementation guidance: Documentation of Security Testing Procedures: Outline your organization's approach to integrating automated security tests, specifying the tools used (e.g., GitHub Advanced Security, OWASP ZAP) and the frequency of these tests. Sample Security Test Reports: Provide recent reports from SAST, DAST, or SCA tools that detail identified vulnerabilities and the steps taken to address them. CI/CD Pipeline Integration Evidence: Show how security testing tools are incorporated into your continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipeline, ensuring that code is automatically scanned for vulnerabilities during development. Access to Security Dashboards: Offer access to dashboards or platforms where ongoing security testing results are displayed, demonstrating continuous monitoring and management of security risks. Training Records: Document training sessions or materials provided to development teams on the importance and implementation of automated security testing practices. Implementation guidance Identify and deploy appropriate SAST, DAST, and SCA tools that align with your tech stack. Start with pilot integrations in your CI/CD pipeline so that security scans run automatically as part of your development process (e.g., on pull requests or scheduled builds). Create a simple reference guide that outlines which tools are used, how they are configured, and where results are stored. Save example scan reports and screenshots of dashboards to demonstrate coverage and activity. Provide basic training to your developers and engineers on how to interpret scan results and address findings. Review your testing setup regularly to ensure it stays aligned with changes in code, dependencies, or infrastructure. Evidence collection Evidence for this control would be collected by demonstrating how automated security testing is implemented and maintained within your application or infrastructure, specifically covering Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA). Document the organization’s security testing procedures, including tools used, test types, frequency, and responsible teams. Gather recent sample reports from SAST, DAST, and SCA tools that show vulnerabilities identified and any remediation actions taken. Provide documentation or screenshots showing how testing tools are integrated into the CI/CD pipeline, including trigger points (e.g., pull requests, nightly builds). Offer access to or screenshots of security dashboards that display ongoing results, trends, or alerting mechanisms related to automated security scans. Collect training records or materials provided to developers or engineering teams on secure coding practices and use of automated testing tools. Ensure all evidence maps clearly to SAST, DAST, and SCA activities, with distinctions made for each category to support audit traceability.

tests.title: Mobile code checked for vulnerabilities
tests.description: Mobile code checked for vulnerabilities
tests.evidenceGuidance: Screenshot, ticket or other evidence that mobile or other browser or endpoint-run code such as javascript, ActiveX, Postscript, VBscript etc that is developed by the company is scanned for vulnerabilities before being deployed in production or shared with customers. Implementation guidance Identify and deploy a vulnerability scanning tool that supports your mobile code types (e.g., JavaScript, ActiveX). Research available solutions and choose one that integrates into your development process, then assign a team member to oversee its configuration. Integrate the tool into your code deployment process so that scans automatically run during code reviews or as part of your CI/CD pipeline. Ensure each scan generates a report with timestamps and details about any vulnerabilities detected. Set up a documentation system to archive the scan reports, tickets, and meeting notes. This system should clearly record when and by whom the security review was conducted, ensuring you can readily retrieve evidence for future compliance requests. Evidence collection To collect evidence that mobile code is checked for vulnerabilities, gather documentation showing that the code is scanned for security issues before deployment. Obtain screenshots or reports from vulnerability scanning tools used on the code. Collect tickets or logs from the issue tracking system showing the review and resolution of identified vulnerabilities. Compile records of code review meetings or approvals indicating security checks were performed. Ensure documentation includes timestamps and responsible personnel for accountability.

controls.title: Outsourced development
controls.description: The organization shall direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development. Company has an approved Secure Development Policy Company has an approved Third-Party Management Policy

tests.title: Outsourced development contract
tests.description: Outsourced development contract
tests.evidenceGuidance: Provide documented evidence demonstrating that the organization directs, monitors, and reviews outsourced system development activities. Examples of evidence can include: Contracts, agreements, or SLAs with third-party developers that specify security, quality, and compliance expectations. Records of oversight activities, such as status reports, meeting minutes, or audit logs reviewing outsourced development progress. Security assessments, code reviews, or penetration testing results performed on outsourced development work. Corrective actions or follow-ups directed to the outsourced development team to address identified risks or non-compliance issues. Implementation guidance Outline key security, quality, and compliance standards needed in contracts or SLAs with third-party developers. Also decide on oversight metrics (e.g., regular status reports, meeting minutes) and technical reviews like security assessments or code reviews. Integrate these requirements into formal contract language and internal procedures. Establish scheduled checkpoints (meetings or reports) to review performance, and plan regular technical assessments to verify adherence to the standards. Begin collecting and archiving contracts, reports, review outcomes, and records of any corrective actions. This documentation will serve as evidence for ongoing management of outsourced development activities. Evidence collection To collect evidence for the management of outsourced system development activities, focus on documentation-based evidence.
